differences.what: THE TWO RIDGE STACKS STOOD TOO FAR INBOARD. Andreas/Braunhold draws both main-block stacks close to the ridge ends — the near one immediately behind the visible gable peak, the far one well out toward the far end — while the model placed them at the generic 0.22/0.78 frontage fractions, about 1.6 m inboard of the picture's disposition on each side. The existing `gable_ends` kit is now selected, so on the retained 9.92 m block their centres are 0.60 m and 9.32 m. Measured on this same camera, the near stack's offset from the gable peak falls from about 0.19 to 0.08 of the visible ridge run against the picture's 0.04, and the far stack's rises from 0.57 to 0.67 against the picture's 0.65. The 0.60 m inset, the 0.90 m square shaft and the ridge + 0.55 m top are reconstructed generator choices; the plate supports the relative disposition and supplies no measurement. docs/LIBERTIES.md L-sauganash-ridge-end-stacks-2383.

The stacks' own proportions and heads still differ from the picture. Andreas draws slender brick shafts standing well clear of the ridge with a corbelled cap; the model carries squat 0.90 m square blocks ridge + 0.55 m with a plain top, which a visitor on the street would notice. Count (2), brick material and the ridge line are unchanged and are not in question. Only the along-ridge station moved here; shaft section, height and cap remain open on their own merits.

THE BOXED GABLE CORNICE AND ITS RETURNS. Andreas/Braunhold draws a boxed band following both rakes of the visible main gable and a short horizontal return turning the corner at each eaves end; the model had a bare rake there, which a visitor on the street would notice. Both are now built on the +x gable in the wall finish, hanging below the rake line. The three sections are reconstructed working choices, not measurements, and the picture's own scale datum supports a return anywhere in roughly 0.55-0.9 m; the remaining section uncertainty is within tolerance under T-3153. Occurrence on the opposite, unseen gable is not claimed and nothing is built there. docs/LIBERTIES.md L-sauganash-main-gable-cornice-2383.

The main and left compound roof silhouette, including the broad rear-left wing, differs visibly from Andreas in the actual current two-building comparison. Existing geometry and surveyed placement are retained. The inherited annex fit does not supply independent hotel dimensions, and this material shape/proportion review remains open.

The left main-gable opening presentation and the model's roof/wall intersections require further whole-hotel review. Do not infer a missing opening count or a new metric set-out from the poorly constrained annex framing. This first hotel comparison does not qualify those details.

The retained annex framing has a low eye and near-edge principal and remains diagnostic. Its camera/pixel-fit uncertainty is within tolerance under T-3153 and adds no independent-calibration sign-off requirement. It supplies no new hotel dimension or historical viewpoint; the observable roof/compound and left-gable differences remain open on their own merits.

The actual current group shows the retained five upper front windows, four lower front windows and central entrance. These counts were already built by earlier merged work; this comparison enrolls them without a geometry change or a new July-1835 dating claim.

The monochrome engraving does not establish a literal green roof, blue shutters or photometric wall finish. Existing declared reconstruction and separate written/coloured-source evidence remain controlling; no material or paint value changes here.

This isolated group omits app terrain, streets, people and surrounding buildings. It does not establish ground contact, walking access, a historical street camera or the original ticket's full picture coverage. Actual published application review is a separate release requirement.
